jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Great Question:

Great Question is the end-to-end agentic user research platform. Our platform enables teams to recruit participants, run research, and share insights – all in one place. Backed by world-class investors and trusted by industry-leading teams like Gusto, Experian, Canva, and Brex, we’re building the future of customer research.

We believe AI is a multiplier for creativity, speed, and scale. Everyone on the team is encouraged to lean into AI, not just to be more efficient, but to push boundaries and unlock new possibilities. Whether you’re writing, designing, coding, or analyzing, we expect you to explore how AI can elevate your craft.

Our culture is built on high trust, high agency, and high emotional intelligence. If you’re looking for a place where your voice matters, where work is fun, and where you're empowered to do your best - join us in redefining user research 🚀

About This Role:

You’ll be a Product Manager owning a strategic area of Great Question with a team of 3–4 engineers. We’ll give you a clear outcome to move. Figuring out the bets that get us there, and the near-term roadmap for your area, is your job. You’ll work alongside two other strong PMs and a product designer, and report to our Head of Product. It’s an individual contributor role, remote in North America with Pacific-hours overlap.

Here’s the kind of problem you might own. Research is a chain of multi-step workflows – recruiting, scheduling, running sessions, synthesis. We want that chain simple and reliable enough that a builder, or an agent working for them, can run it end to end in a flexible way. That’s harder than it sounds.

In your first three months, you’ll take over an area tied to our strategy, ship a few meaningful things with your team, and find out whether they worked.

What this role isn’t: managing a backlog or running process. You’ll move between strategy and execution all the time, and you’ll own the results your area is meant to drive.

What You’ll Be Responsible For:

  1. Find the bet. Dig through product data and customer signals – support chats, sales asks, your own research – and come back with a strong hypothesis about what will move your outcome.

  2. Shape it. Sometimes that means scoping the problem carefully. Sometimes it means skipping straight to a prototype. Part of the job is knowing which. Then decide what happens now, later or never.

  3. Ship it well. Keep the team organized and motivated, and stay close enough to the details that it ships on time and to a high bar.

  4. Release it. Run the launch and make sure Sales, Success and Marketing know what’s coming and have what they need.

  5. Learn from it. Watch what happens, then decide whether to double down, iterate or stop.

About You:

  • 5+ years as a product manager in B2B software.

  • You’re as comfortable in product analytics or a database query as you are on a customer call. You form strong opinions and change them when the evidence does.

  • You stay in the details, and you’ve shipped complex work on time without lowering the bar.

  • You use AI tools like Claude Code or Cursor every day, and you’ve shipped AI features yourself – MCP servers, agentic workflows – that held up in production.

You’ll thrive here if you’re:

  • Bought in on AI. You’re excited about it. You try new tools constantly, keep up with what’s possible, and can tell where AI helps and where it just adds noise.

  • Technical enough to be dangerous. You use AI to get hands-on, whether that’s shipping a small fix or prototyping something in code.

  • Close to customers. You talk to customers regularly and it shows up in your decisions.

  • Clear and decisive. You communicate clearly, make the call, and commit.

  • High agency. You see what needs doing and do it without waiting to be asked. You push through the hard parts and finish what you start, without letting quality slip.

Bonus points

  • You’ve worked on B2B workflow products, especially multi-step flows where state and status get complicated.

  • You’ve worked hands-on with agent runtimes, or measured the quality of AI output.

  • You’ve been on a remote, async team before.

This is a fun problem for product people

If you’ve been a PM or designer for a while, you’ve shipped something without enough customer signal and wondered afterward if you got it right. That’s the problem we work on.

You’ll get to throw the newest AI capabilities at it, and a lot of what we’re building wasn’t possible a year ago. Nobody has figured out how builders can seamlessly incorporate customer signal into the dozens of decisions they make each week. It is a real chance to innovate.

How we work

We’re a small, senior team. You’ll own an area end to end, and we care more about what changed for customers than about what shipped.

Product, design and engineering work closely together, and everyone stays close to customers. We’re remote, so we write things down and lean on async.

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

  • A culture of customer obsession and curiosity

  • Opportunity to shape and scale a critical business function

  • Remote-first culture with high trust and high autonomy

  • Annual team retreats and virtual events

  • Opportunity to work on cutting-edge AI integrations that matter

  • Competitive compensation & equity

  • Generous PTO, health benefits, and learning stipend

Equal Opportunity Statement

Great Question is committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination or harassment. We expect every member of the Great Question community to do their part to cultivate and maintain an environment where everyone has the opportunity to feel included, and is afforded the respect and dignity they deserve.

Decisions related to hiring, compensating, training, evaluating performance, or terminating are made fairly, and we provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified candidates and employees. We examine our unconscious biases and take responsibility for always striving to create an inclusive environment that makes every employee and candidate feel welcome.

jobs.title: Product Engineer (AI / Full-Stack)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Great Question:

Great Question is the end-to-end agentic user research platform. Our platform enables teams to recruit participants, run research, and share insights – all in one place. Backed by world-class investors and trusted by industry-leading teams like Gusto, Experian, Canva, and Brex, we’re building the future of customer research.

We believe AI is a multiplier for creativity, speed, and scale. Everyone on the team is encouraged to lean into AI, not just to be more efficient, but to push boundaries and unlock new possibilities. Whether you’re writing, designing, coding, or analyzing, we expect you to explore how AI can elevate your craft.

Our culture is built on high trust, high agency, and high emotional intelligence. If you’re looking for a place where your voice matters, where work is fun, and where you're empowered to do your best - join us in redefining user research 🚀

Product Engineer (Full-Stack) — Canada, Remote

 

I’m PJ, CTO at Great Question. My co-founder Ned and I built this company on a simple idea: talking to your customers should be easy. This has only become more relevant as it’s become faster to build, but validating your ideas is still slow and painful.

Research, design, and product teams at ServiceNow, Brex and Canva run their customer research on us, and we raised a $13M Series A led by Inovia late last year after going through YC in 2021.

This year we’ve been doubling down on the agentic future of research. We’re super excited about what we’ve built and now we need help to continue rebuilding core parts of our product, agent-first. I’m hiring our first Product Engineers in Canada to do it with us.

The role

Product Engineer here means you take a problem and run with it end to end - from the customer conversation to production to validating whether it actually worked. PM support is light and as-required: a PM helps size the problem, shape the appetite, and call priority, but nobody hands you a spec. From there you're trusted to find the right solution, because you're close to the customer and you have great product sense. That only works with people who are self-directed and genuinely value autonomy and accountability.

You'll build across the product stack - from Rails APIs and React/TypeScript frontends to video streaming, realtime voice agents, agentic search, product analytics, and everything in between - working directly with the founders, our designer, and the rest of engineering.

What we're looking for

How you work. AI is embedded across your entire workflow - not just used for coding. You might spend a morning digging through interview transcripts and product analytics to understand a problem, build a few throwaway prototypes to see which approach holds up, and then build a technical plan before handing it to a couple of agents to build and QA.

We’re expecting great judgment around all of that: breaking work into sensible pieces, evaluating the output carefully, and most importantly, owning whatever ships, regardless of who typed it.

What you build. You build highly usable, customer-centric products that people love. You take the extra time to really dig into the data to make sure you understand the problem; and validate that what you’ve built actually solves it. You’ll go the extra mile to deliver something with UI + UX polish, while also thinking in systems to make sure that you’re using the right primitives so you’re delivering less bespoke solutions.

Who you are. We're a small team of exceptional engineers, and we only hire people who raise the bar.

  • Strong across the full stack. An expert in both exposing APIs and the frontend it sits upon. We’re a Rails and TypeScript team, but it’s not a hard requirement.

  • Built and run production systems. Shipping features live and then maintaining them long enough to see what works (and what doesn’t!)

  • Live in an agentic coding harness daily (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor - we don't care which) and have real opinions about your setup.

  • Ideally shipped LLM-powered features, or least know what it takes to run them in production.

  • Have shipped things where you decided what to build, and can defend your UX opinions.

  • Write clearly. We're remote and async-heavy; people who write clearly think (and prompt) clearly.

  • Are senior (roughly 5+ years with real ownership). Our level grading is tougher than most.

How we build

We've rebuilt how we work around AI agents, to ensure our engineers are unblocked to work at AI native speeds:

  • Main goes to production and approvals aren’t always required. Fast, automated CI is the gate, and we trust people to make the right judgements. Good work goes live as soon as it’s finished.

  • We invest in making the codebase easy to work in: written runbooks and conventions that help agents and new people find their way around quickly.

  • Running a few agents in parallel is easy, and expected. Sandboxes and preview environments are trivial to spawn.

  • You'll always have the latest tools and models, and we're generous with tokens.

  • Light on ceremony, high on accountability and communication.

This might not be for everyone, but if it excites you, please apply. We’re especially keen to meet people who are willing to challenge some of these ideas with their own hard-won lessons from the arena.

Your first 90 days

We expect you to hit the ground running, and fast.

  • Week 1: use the harness to learn the codebase and merge your first PR, ideally on day one. You’re deep in the customer data, in their Slack channels, and solving problems.

  • First 30 days: ship into a live area. That might be AI Moderator quality, or working directly on our global chat experience. You understand the product, the competitors, the problems we’re solving, and have a view on how we can win.

  • By 60 days: You own a surface - how the research agent communicates findings, growing our MCP surface, or rebuilding a core page on the new design system.

  • By 90 days: you're deep on a product area: talking to its customers, deciding what's next, accountable for whether it worked. You’re pushing the strategy with the founders & Head of Product in new directions with confidence.

Who shouldn't apply

  • Ambiguity and shifting priorities wear you down. Problems arrive here half-shaped, and the roadmap has changed under our feet more than once this year. Some people find that energizing; if you don't, you'll hate it.

  • You wait to be unblocked. We’re a small team, remote, and with light processes… resourcefulness is critical to the job. We need people who unblock themselves.

  • You’re not all-in on AI. Dabbling won't cut it here. Agents are how we work, not a thing we're trying out.

  • You'd rather not talk to customers. Product engineers here get on calls, read transcripts, and sit in the support queue sometimes. That closeness is the whole point of the role.

  • You only want the shiny work. Plenty of weeks are polish, reliability, and making something 5% less annoying.

  • You want a PM to frame the problem and hand you a spec. “Just tell me what to build and I’ll build it” will not fly here.

Benefits

  • Full-time employment with proper benefits, generous salary in CAD.

  • Remote, anywhere in Canada. We generally work PST hours, but are flexible.

  • 4 weeks PTO

  • Annual team offsite (this year is San Diego!)

  • Brand new Macbook pro

  • Enough tokens that you'll never be left wanting

  • Freedom to use the latest technologies and vendors

A note on compensation: Our offers sit in a defined band for the level, and set by our internal leveling rubric (scope of ownership, technical depth, previous relevant experience), not by negotiation. Most offers land near the midpoint.

Our interview process

  1. Intro call w/ Cofounder/CTO (30 min). Your story, what you've shipped. Our story, the impact you can have here.

  2. Quality session (~ 60 min). Do you know what quality looks like - both in terms of product and code.

  3. Building session (~90 min). Build something real in our domain with your own AI tooling, the way you actually work; we walk through the code together as you go. We reimburse AI credits.

  4. Team + values (~60 min) . Meet the people you'll work with and ensure we all see the world the same way.

  5. Founder conversation (~30 min). Meet the CEO.

  6. References, then offer.

No leetcode. AI tools aren't just allowed - they're expected just as they are in the job.

How to apply

Send a link to something you've built that real people are using - and a few sentences on why you’re interested in this role.

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

  • A culture of customer obsession and curiosity

  • Opportunity to shape and scale a critical business function

  • Remote-first culture with high trust and high autonomy

  • Annual team retreats and virtual events

  • Opportunity to work on cutting-edge AI integrations that matter

  • Competitive compensation & equity

  • Generous PTO, health benefits, and learning stipend

Equal Opportunity Statement

Great Question is committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination or harassment. We expect every member of the Great Question community to do their part to cultivate and maintain an environment where everyone has the opportunity to feel included, and is afforded the respect and dignity they deserve.

Decisions related to hiring, compensating, training, evaluating performance, or terminating are made fairly, and we provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified candidates and employees. We examine our unconscious biases and take responsibility for always striving to create an inclusive environment that makes every employee and candidate feel welcome.

Backed by world-class investors and trusted by industry-leading teams like Gusto, Experian, Canva, and Brex, we’re building the future of customer research.

I’m PJ, CTO at Great Question. My co-founder Ned and I built this company on a simple idea: talking to your customers should be easy. That’s only become more relevant as building gets faster, but validating your ideas is still slow and painful.

This year we’ve been rebuilding core parts of our product agent-first, and the engineering team is growing to match. I’m hiring an Engineering Manager to lead two of the teams at the center of that work.

THE ROLE

As Engineering Manager, you’ll lead our Methods and Insights teams and report to Marcelo, our Director of Engineering. Alongside our Research Operations team, these are the pillar teams behind most of the product. Methods powers every study and the experience participants see; Insights makes sense of the data and helps customers act on it.

The job has three parts, and we need all of them:

  • People. Hiring and staffing, 1:1s, coaching, feedback, performance management and growth. You're the person your engineers trust to tell them the truth about their work, and to push hard for their growth.

  • Delivery and operations (trains on time). You run the cycle for your teams: planning, sequencing, unblocking, managing risk and working with stakeholders, and you lead the change as we evolve how we build. You make sure what we committed to actually ships, at a quality we're proud of, and you own your teams' operational health once it's live, from monitoring to red-teaming.

  • Building the factory. Our engineers each run several agents, so the slow part is no longer writing code. It’s specs, review and judgment. How you deliver. jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Great Question:

Great Question is the end-to-end agentic user research platform. Our platform enables teams to recruit participants, run research, and share insights – all in one place. Backed by world-class investors and trusted by industry-leading teams like Gusto, Experian, Canva, and Brex, we’re building the future of customer research.

We believe AI is a multiplier for creativity, speed, and scale. Everyone on the team is encouraged to lean into AI, not just to be more efficient, but to push boundaries and unlock new possibilities. Whether you’re writing, designing, coding, or analyzing, we expect you to explore how AI can elevate your craft.

Our culture is built on high trust, high agency, and high emotional intelligence. If you’re looking for a place where your voice matters, where work is fun, and where you're empowered to do your best - join us in redefining user research 🚀

About This Role:

You’ll be a Product Manager owning a strategic area of Great Question with a team of 3–4 engineers. We’ll give you a clear outcome to move. Figuring out the bets that get us there, and the near-term roadmap for your area, is your job. You’ll work alongside two other strong PMs and a product designer, and report to our Head of Product. It’s an individual contributor role, remote in North America with Pacific-hours overlap.

Here’s the kind of problem you might own. Research is a chain of multi-step workflows – recruiting, scheduling, running sessions, synthesis. We want that chain simple and reliable enough that a builder, or an agent working for them, can run it end to end in a flexible way. That’s harder than it sounds.

In your first three months, you’ll take over an area tied to our strategy, ship a few meaningful things with your team, and find out whether they worked.

What this role isn’t: managing a backlog or running process. You’ll move between strategy and execution all the time, and you’ll own the results your area is meant to drive.

What You’ll Be Responsible For:

  1. Find the bet. Dig through product data and customer signals – support chats, sales asks, your own research – and come back with a strong hypothesis about what will move your outcome.

  2. Shape it. Sometimes that means scoping the problem carefully. Sometimes it means skipping straight to a prototype. Part of the job is knowing which. Then decide what happens now, later or never.

  3. Ship it well. Keep the team organized and motivated, and stay close enough to the details that it ships on time and to a high bar.

  4. Release it. Run the launch and make sure Sales, Success and Marketing know what’s coming and have what they need.

  5. Learn from it. Watch what happens, then decide whether to double down, iterate or stop.

About You:

  • 5+ years as a product manager in B2B software.

  • You’re as comfortable in product analytics or a database query as you are on a customer call. You form strong opinions and change them when the evidence does.

  • You stay in the details, and you’ve shipped complex work on time without lowering the bar.

  • You use AI tools like Claude Code or Cursor every day, and you’ve shipped AI features yourself – MCP servers, agentic workflows – that held up in production.

You’ll thrive here if you’re:

  • Bought in on AI. You’re excited about it. You try new tools constantly, keep up with what’s possible, and can tell where AI helps and where it just adds noise.

  • Technical enough to be dangerous. You use AI to get hands-on, whether that’s shipping a small fix or prototyping something in code.

  • Close to customers. You talk to customers regularly and it shows up in your decisions.

  • Clear and decisive. You communicate clearly, make the call, and commit.

  • High agency. You see what needs doing and do it without waiting to be asked. You push through the hard parts and finish what you start, without letting quality slip.

Bonus points

  • You’ve worked on B2B workflow products, especially multi-step flows where state and status get complicated.

  • You’ve worked hands-on with agent runtimes, or measured the quality of AI output.

  • You’ve been on a remote, async team before.

This is a fun problem for product people

If you’ve been a PM or designer for a while, you’ve shipped something without enough customer signal and wondered afterward if you got it right. That’s the problem we work on.

You’ll get to throw the newest AI capabilities at it, and a lot of what we’re building wasn’t possible a year ago. Nobody has figured out how builders can seamlessly incorporate customer signal into the dozens of decisions they make each week. It is a real chance to innovate.

How we work

We’re a small, senior team. You’ll own an area end to end, and we care more about what changed for customers than about what shipped.

Product, design and engineering work closely together, and everyone stays close to customers. We’re remote, so we write things down and lean on async.

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

  • A culture of customer obsession and curiosity

  • Opportunity to shape and scale a critical business function

  • Remote-first culture with high trust and high autonomy

  • Annual team retreats and virtual events

  • Opportunity to work on cutting-edge AI integrations that matter

  • Competitive compensation & equity

  • Generous PTO, health benefits, and learning stipend

Equal Opportunity Statement

Great Question is committed to providing a workplace free from discrimination or harassment. We expect every member of the Great Question community to do their part to cultivate and maintain an environment where everyone has the opportunity to feel included, and is afforded the respect and dignity they deserve.

Decisions related to hiring, compensating, training, evaluating performance, or terminating are made fairly, and we provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified candidates and employees. We examine our unconscious biases and take responsibility for always striving to create an inclusive environment that makes every employee and candidate feel welcome.

About This Role

Great Question is on a mission to democratize user research. We're a well-funded startup backed by Y Combinator and FundersClub, looking for a driven, coachable Business Development Representative with B2B sales experience to join our fully remote team.

You'll get in early, work on an interesting problem, and have a real impact on both the product and the culture of an early-stage company, while helping shape how teams use research to build software.

BDRs drive revenue by creating pipeline. You'll find the right people at mid-market and enterprise companies who would benefit from our research automation platform, and connect them with our Account Executives.

To succeed here, you'll need the discipline to work independently and either a passion for the research space or the drive to learn it quickly.

This role is remote and open to candidates in the US and Canada.

How to apply: Do the job to get the job. Apply on our website, then find Won You, our hiring manager, and pitch him on a screener call. Tell him why you're a fit and why it's worth his time. Applications without outreach won't be reviewed.

What You'll Do

  • Prospecting & Lead Generation: Book meetings on target accounts through multi-channel, multi-threaded outreach across phone, LinkedIn and email. Cold calling is your top priority channel, with a minimum of 100 dials a day, so you should be comfortable on the phone. Our Demand Gen builds the lists, sequences and workflows with you, and you'll write manual, personalized outreach where an account calls for it.

  • Qualifying & Handing Off: Book meetings that meet our qualification bar and brief the Account Executive so they walk in knowing the pain, the stakeholders and the timeline.

  • Keeping HubSpot Clean: Log every call, disposition and next step, because our routing and reporting run on it.

  • Bringing Back What You Hear: Share what you learn on calls about copy, outbound approach and channels, and come back with a recommendation on what to change.

About You

  • Sales experience: 1–3 years in sales, ideally selling SaaS to B2B or enterprise customers. You have a quota you can name and attainment you can walk us through, misses included.

  • Comfortable on the phone at volume: You know your own connect rate and conversation-to-meeting rate.

  • Analytical and systematic: You own the outcome. When something isn't working, you figure out why and come back with a recommendation.

  • Coachable: You're always looking to get better, and you can tell us about coaching that changed how you work.

  • Competitive and team-first: You're driven to beat your own numbers and invested in the team hitting its goal.

  • Self-directed: You stay disciplined working remotely at an early-stage company and solve problems before being asked.

  • AI-native: You use Claude or ChatGPT beyond the chat window, such as Claude Code or similar tools, to do your job faster, and you can tell us how.

Nice to Have

  • Startup experience: You've worked at an early-stage company.

Our Interview Process

  1. Get our attention. Apply, then reach Won and sell him on having a screener call with you.

  2. Hiring manager interview (30-minutes). Get to know each other and the role.

  3. Assessment + mock cold call (45-minutes). Show us what you learned about Great Question and how you'd break into one target account, then make a mock cold call.

  4. Final (60-minutes split into 2 30-minute sessions). Meet Harri, our Chief of Staff who oversees the Demand Gen function, and Tucker, our Director of Revenue who oversees Sales.

Each interview is sequential, and you'll hear from us within 48 hours of each one.
